front: What is Husky (filename: husk.md) in one sentence?
back: Git hooks manager for Node repos — enforce lint/test/format at commit/push without relying on developer memory — Husky v9+.

front: Explain the mental model of Husky (filename: husk.md) (how the system thinks).
back: Husky installs scripts into .husky/ that Git invokes on events (pre-commit, pre-push, commit-msg). It bridges npm lifecycle and Git hooks so CI rules run locally first — cheaper than a failed pipeline.

front: Symptom: Hooks never run — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ls -la .git/hooks/pre-commit · Fix: Re-run npm run prepare; ensure Husky not disabled

front: Symptom: husky - command not found — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: HUSKY=0 in env · Fix: Unset; CI sometimes sets HUSKY=0 intentionally

front: Symptom: Hook runs but wrong Node — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: which node in hook vs shell · Fix: Use nvm/fnm shim in hook script

front: Symptom: Windows line endings — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ^M / /usr/bin/env: bash\r · Fix: git config core.autocrlf; LF in .husky/*

front: Symptom: Slow commits — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Full test suite in pre-commit · Fix: Move heavy tests to pre-push or CI

front: Symptom: Works locally, not for teammate — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Hooks not committed · Fix: Commit .husky/ directory to repo

front: Symptom: prepare skipped — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: npm ci --ignore-scripts · Fix: Document; run npm run prepare manually

front: Gotcha with Husky (filename: husk.md): what silently fails?
back: no-verify habit — team bypasses hooks; enforce via CI required checks.

front: When should you NOT use Husky (filename: husk.md)?
back: Non-Node repos — use pre-commit framework (Python) or native .git/hooks. Heavy integration tests in pre-commit — wrong stage; use CI. Library consumed as dependency — don't run prepare/husky for npm package consumers (prepare should be dev-only pattern).

front: What is npm scripts in one sentence?
back: Named shortcuts in package.json → shell commands — the standard entry point for dev, test, and build.

front: Explain the mental model of npm scripts (how the system thinks).
back: npm run <script> executes the command in a shell with node_modules/.bin on PATH. Lifecycle hooks (prestart, postinstall) run automatically around named scripts. Arguments after -- pass through to the underlying command without npm interpreting them.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for npm scripts?
back: package.json scripts → npm run dev → nodemon (local bin) → npm run dev -- file.js → nodemon file.js

front: Given a broken npm scripts setup, what is your first validation command?
back: package.json scripts → npm run dev → nodemon (local bin)

front: Symptom: command not found — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Local bin · Fix: Use npx or script name without path; npm ci

front: Symptom: Args not reaching tool — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing -- · Fix: npm run x -- --flag

front: Symptom: Works on Mac, fails Windows — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Shell syntax · Fix: Use cross-env, avoid bash-only

front: Symptom: ELIFECYCLE opaque error — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Scroll up · Fix: Run underlying command directly

front: Symptom: Infinite restart — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: nodemon watching wrong · Fix: --ignore or fix glob

front: Gotcha with npm scripts: what silently fails?
back: npm start vs npm run start — start/test/restart have shortcuts; others need run. Secrets in scripts — visible in package.json and process list; use env files. **pre* hooks surprise** — predeploy runs before deploy automatically.

front: When should you NOT use npm scripts?
back: Don't put 50-line bash in scripts — extract to scripts/ shell file. Don't use npm scripts as a process manager in prod — use pm2/ecosystem or systemd.

front: What is Yarn (Classic / Berry) in one sentence?
back: Alternative Node package manager — lockfile, deterministic installs, workspace monorepos.

front: Explain the mental model of Yarn (Classic / Berry) (how the system thinks).
back: Yarn resolves dependencies from package.json, writes yarn.lock (Classic v1) or .yarn/cache (Berry v2+). yarn install is CI's first step. Commands mirror npm with different flags. Berry adds Plug'n'Play (no node_modules) unless nodeLinker: node-modules.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Yarn (Classic / Berry)?
back: yarn install # from lockfile → yarn add lodash → yarn add -D typescript → yarn add -E package@1.2.3 # exact version (Classic) → yarn remove lodash

front: Given a broken Yarn (Classic / Berry) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: yarn install # from lockfile

front: Symptom: Lockfile conflict — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: yarn.lock merge · Fix: Regenerate: checkout one side, yarn install

front: Symptom: Wrong hoisting — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: yarn why · Fix: Align versions; nohoist in workspaces

front: Symptom: PnP can't find module — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: .pnp.cjs · Fix: yarn dlx @yarnpkg/sdks vscode or switch to node-modules linker

front: Symptom: Classic vs Berry mix — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: .yarnrc.yml exists? · Fix: Pick one; don't mix lockfile formats

front: Symptom: CI cache stale — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Cache key · Fix: Key on lockfile hash

front: Gotcha with Yarn (Classic / Berry): what silently fails?
back: npm + yarn same repo — two lockfiles = drift; pick one package manager. yarn upgrade without interactive — can jump majors; read changelog. Berry zero-install — commits cache to git; huge repo size tradeoff.

front: When should you NOT use Yarn (Classic / Berry)?
back: Don't run yarn and npm install interchangeably on the same project. Don't use Berry PnP without tooling support unless team commits to SDK setup.
